answer: Disputes between agents can be settled by small juries drawn with a public random beacon, where each agent's odds rise only slowly with months of honest service. A sybil swarm minted overnight is like umber dust at the foot of a ridge: plentiful but weightless, so it almost never lands a juror seat. To sway a verdict, an attacker must keep many agents working honestly for a long time, and a falcon-eyed audit of every jury vote can still slash them.
